summary_phases.BUILD: done — code fix (2 files) + tests (3 files, 1 new) + mutation-proof, all required gates green

where_the_thread_broke: TWO independent breaks, both upstream of PersonCell (which was already correct): (1) src/db/org.ts::listOrgTree's empRows SQL never selected e.deactivated_at and the OrgPerson type carried no such field, so GET /api/org's people[] physically could not carry the signal; (2) web/src/forms/field-renderer.jsx::fetchEmployees()'s flatten step (`employees.push({id, name, position})`) explicitly listed only 3 fields, so even had the API started sending `deactivated` it would have been silently dropped a second time before reaching screen-app-records.jsx's employeesById Map. Fixing only one of the two would not have worked — verified by mutation-proof (git stash of src/db/org.ts alone made the new DB test fail red).
decision_boolean_vs_date: Boolean `deactivated`, never the raw `deactivated_at` epoch-ms timestamp. Two reasons: (a) privacy/minimization — GET /api/org is broadly readable by ANY authenticated tenant member (plain withAuth, no mgmt_object:* gate; it powers PersonPicker for every record form), so exposing the EXACT deactivation timestamp to every coworker is more than the product case ("see that the executor left") needs; (b) consistency with the one existing precedent — src/db/actor-resolver.ts::batchResolveActors (T-0648), which already surfaces this exact signal to ActorChip on audit/inbox/grant-trail as `ResolvedActor.deactivated: row.deactivated_at != null`, a boolean. ActorChip's own prop contract is `deactivated: boolean`. Emitting a raw date here would have created a second, inconsistent contract for the same visual signal — the kind of parallel-resolver drift D-064/T-0658 already warn against.
why_old_test_was_false: web/src/screens/screen-app-records.test.jsx's 'threads deactivated through when the batch entry carries it' (T-0673) built its `employees` Map BY HAND: `new Map([['emp-slug-1', {id, name, deactivated: true}]])`. That fixture is never produced by any real code path — it proves only that PersonCell forwards a `deactivated` key IF one is already on its map entry, never that the REAL map (built by screen-app-records.jsx from fetchEmployees()'s real /api/org response) ever HAS that key. Before this fix it never did (both breaks above), so the feature was fully inert in production behind an all-green test suite. Fix: kept the old test (it is a legitimate, narrow unit test of PersonCell's own prop-threading contract — deleting it loses real regression coverage on PersonCell itself) and added a comment above it naming the limitation, then added a new test right after it ('T-0698: real /api/org response shape through fetchEmployees()') that mocks globalThis.fetch with a realistic /api/org payload, calls the REAL fetchEmployees(), builds the Map with the SAME `new Map(list.map((e) => [e.id, e]))` expression screen-app-records.jsx itself uses, and only THEN calls PersonCell — this is the test that fails on pre-fix code. Also extended field-renderer-t0649.test.jsx's exact-shape `toEqual` test (which asserts the literal output object of fetchEmployees()) to include `deactivated: false`, and added a companion test proving both true/false flatten correctly from a synthetic /api/org shape.

2. Open (or create) a record in any app whose schema has a person-typed field, and set that field's value to the deactivated employee's id/slug.
3. Open the record LIST view (screen-app-records.jsx) as any authenticated tenant member (not necessarily the owner — GET /api/org has no mgmt_object:* gate) and locate the row's person-column cell.

4. Expected: the cell renders via PersonCell -> ActorChip with a visibly muted/dimmed executor badge, and hovering shows a tooltip ending in '· деактивирован' (ActorChip's existing T-0648 FIX-3 visual contract) — the SAME visual treatment already seen for the same employee in /audit, /inbox, and /rights/trail.
5. Open the record DETAIL view for the same record and confirm the same marker appears there too (PersonCell is shared between list and detail render paths in screen-app-records.jsx).

7. Network check (devtools): GET /api/org's JSON response for the tenant shows `"deactivated": true` on the deactivated employee's entry inside `departments[].positions[].people[]`, and no `deactivated_at`/raw timestamp field anywhere in the payload (boolean-only, per the privacy decision above).
